weeks.goal: Get your hands back on Python, and learn to price an algorithm before you write it.
d: Setup: VS Code, Python 3.12, LeetCode + GFG accounts. Variables, I/O, f-strings, type casting.
Sum of first N, reverse a number, count digits, palindrome number, Armstrong number.
What HTML actually is. Document structure, head vs body, semantic tags: header, nav, main, section, article, footer.
Conditionals, while vs for, range(), nested loops, break/continue.
Striver pattern problems 1–8 (rectangle, right triangle, inverted triangle, pyramid).
Text elements, lists, links, images. Attributes, alt text, absolute vs relative paths.
Functions: parameters, defaults, *args/**kwargs, return vs print, local vs global scope.
Striver patterns 9–15. Then: prime check, GCD by Euclid, LCM.
Forms: input types, labels, select, textarea, button. Tables. Why semantics matter for accessibility.
Big-O: how to count operations. O(1), O(log n), O(n), O(n log n), O(n²), O(2ⁿ). Best/avg/worst.
No new problems today. Go back through every problem you've solved and write its time and space complexity.
Build a semantic CV page from scratch — no CSS at all. Just correct structure.
Space complexity, auxiliary vs total. Recursion stack cost. Python traps: list.insert(0,x) is O(n), 'in' on a list is O(n).
Striver patterns 16–22. Then trailing zeroes in factorial, digit sum, count of digits without loop.
Forms deep-dive: validation attributes, fieldset, accessibility. Add a contact form to the CV page.
Lists: indexing, slicing, mutation, aliasing vs copy vs deepcopy, list comprehensions.
Reverse an array in place, find min and max, second largest without sorting, left rotate by one.
Meta tags, favicon, Open Graph. Validate your page with the W3C validator and fix every warning.
sun: Re-solve the 3 patterns you found hardest, from a blank file, no reference. Then write a Big-O cheat sheet in your own words — one page, no copying.
Core CS: what happens when you run a Python file — interpreter, bytecode, memory. Set up your notes repo on GitHub.

weeks.goal: Learn the Python equivalent of C++ STL. Hashing is the single highest-return tool you'll pick up all year.
d: Dict and set internals: how hashing gives O(1) average lookup, and when it degrades to O(n).
Frequency count of an array, highest and lowest frequency element, count distinct elements.
The cascade, specificity, inheritance. Selectors: type, class, id, descendant, pseudo-class.
Tuples, immutability, strings as sequences. sorted() with key=, lambda, reverse=.
Sort a list of tuples by second element, valid anagram, sort characters by frequency.
The box model: content, padding, border, margin. box-sizing: border-box and why everyone sets it.
collections: Counter, defaultdict, deque, OrderedDict. heapq basics. This is your STL.
Rewrite Monday's and Tuesday's problems using Counter and defaultdict. Compare line counts.
Flexbox properly: flex-direction, justify-content, align-items, gap, flex-grow/shrink/basis.
Basic maths: extracting digits, finding divisors in O(√n), prime check, Sieve of Eratosthenes.
Count digits, print all divisors, check prime, sieve up to 10⁶, GCD by Euclid.
Flexbox practice: navbar, card row, centred hero. Build three layouts from scratch.
Recursion: the call stack, base case, recursion tree. Python's recursion limit and how to raise it.
Print 1 to N, print N to 1, sum of first N, factorial, reverse an array recursively.
Typography and colour: font stacks, web fonts, line-height, letter-spacing, rem vs px vs em.
Parameterised vs functional recursion. Multiple recursive calls and why Fibonacci is exponential.
Check palindrome recursively, Fibonacci, power(x, n) in O(log n) using fast exponentiation.
Style your CV page fully. No frameworks. Make deliberate typography choices.
sun: Re-solve four hashing problems cold. Draw the recursion tree for factorial(5) and fib(5) on paper by hand — count the calls.
Core CS: OOP in Python — class, object, __init__, self, instance vs class attributes.

weeks.goal: Implement every sort by hand once. You'll never implement them at work, but the reasoning transfers everywhere.
d: Selection, bubble, insertion sort. Why each is O(n²). Stability and what it means in practice.
Implement all three from scratch, no reference. Then trace each on [5,2,9,1] on paper.
CSS Grid: grid-template-columns, rows, fr units, gap, grid-area. Grid vs Flexbox — when each wins.
Merge sort: divide and conquer, the merge step, why O(n log n), why it needs O(n) extra space.
Implement merge sort. Then merge two sorted arrays without extra space.
Responsive design: media queries, mobile-first, fluid type with clamp(), container queries.
Quick sort: pivot choice, partition, O(n²) worst case. Why Python's sort() is Timsort.
Implement quick sort. Then find the kth smallest element using partition.
Tailwind: setup, utility classes, responsive prefixes, why utility-first. Rebuild one CV section in Tailwind.
Array traversal patterns. Scanning once vs twice. In-place vs extra space.
Largest element, second largest without sorting, check if array is sorted, remove duplicates from sorted array.
Tailwind continued: custom config, extending the theme, dark mode, @apply and when not to use it.
Rotation: the reversal algorithm and why it beats the naive approach.
Left rotate by one, left rotate by K places, move all zeroes to end, linear search.
Rebuild your whole CV page as a responsive portfolio in Tailwind. Mobile, tablet, desktop.
The XOR trick for finding a missing or single element. Union and intersection of sorted arrays.
Union of two sorted arrays, intersection, missing number, max consecutive ones, single number.
Polish: transitions, hover states, focus-visible rings, prefers-reduced-motion. Ship it.
sun: Re-implement merge sort and quick sort from a blank file. Time yourself. Under 10 minutes each is the target.
Core CS: OOP — inheritance, polymorphism, encapsulation. Write a small class hierarchy in Python.

weeks.goal: Kadane and prefix-sum-with-hashmap are two of the five patterns that carry the whole array section.
d: Two Sum: the brute force, the sorted two-pointer, the hashmap. Know all three and their trade-offs.
Two Sum (all three ways), sort an array of 0s, 1s and 2s (Dutch National Flag).
Git properly: init, add, commit, the staging area, .gitignore, writing commit messages that mean something.
Moore's voting algorithm — the intuition for why cancelling pairs works.
Majority element (> n/2), majority element (> n/3).
Branching: branch, merge, merge conflicts and how to resolve them without panicking. Feature-branch workflow.
Kadane's algorithm: the local-vs-global maximum idea. Prefix sums as a concept.
Maximum subarray sum, print the subarray itself, best time to buy and sell stock.
Remotes: push, pull, fetch, origin. Pull requests. Fork vs clone. Undo: reset, revert, stash.
The prefix-sum-plus-hashmap pattern. Why it handles negative numbers when sliding window can't.
Longest subarray with sum K (positives only), subarray sum equals K, longest subarray with sum K (with negatives).
Deploy the portfolio to GitHub Pages or Vercel. Custom domain if you have one. Get it genuinely live.
In-place rearrangement. Next permutation — the four-step algorithm.
Rearrange array by sign, next permutation, leaders in an array.
README that earns its keep: what it does, screenshot, stack, how to run locally, what you'd do next.
Matrix traversal as index arithmetic: rotation, spiral, in-place marking.
Rotate matrix by 90°, spiral traversal of a matrix, set matrix zeroes.
Clean up your GitHub profile: bio, pinned repos, profile README. Recruiters do look.
sun: Month 1 done. Re-solve Kadane and both prefix-sum problems cold. Update your Excel tracker and check your revision backlog is at zero.
Core CS: OOP — abstraction, dunder methods, when a class is the right tool and when a function is.

weeks.goal: Intervals aren't in Striver's sheet as their own step, but they're asked constantly. We add them here.
d: Pascal's triangle — the three distinct questions hidden in one topic (nth row, single element, full triangle).
Pascal's triangle: all three variants.
JS: let/const/var, types, coercion, ==  vs ===, truthy/falsy. The parts that bite you.
Longest consecutive sequence — why a set turns O(n log n) into O(n).
Longest consecutive sequence, longest subarray with sum K revisited.
Functions, arrow functions, this, scope, closures. Closures matter — take your time here.
The interval pattern: sort by start time, then sweep. Merge condition.
Merge overlapping intervals, insert interval.
Arrays and objects. Destructuring, spread, rest. map / filter / reduce / find / some / every.
Sweep line and non-overlapping selection. Sort-by-end for maximum count.
Non-overlapping intervals, meeting rooms, minimum platforms required.
Objects deeper: prototypes, classes, getters/setters. JSON parse and stringify.
Merge sort applications — counting inversions and reverse pairs during the merge.
Count inversions, reverse pairs.
Modules: import/export. Error handling: try/catch, throw, custom errors. Optional chaining.
Hard array tricks: XOR for repeat-and-missing, Kadane for products, two-pointer for k-sum.
Repeat and missing number, maximum product subarray, 3-Sum, 4-Sum.
Practice day: rewrite three of your Python array solutions in JavaScript. Same logic, different language.
sun: Re-solve 3-Sum and merge intervals cold. Both are pattern anchors you'll reuse a dozen times.
Core CS: month recap. Write blog-style notes on hashing and Kadane in your notes repo.

weeks.goal: The binary search template must become muscle memory. Write it until you can't get it wrong.
d: The template: low, high, mid, and the loop invariant. Why mid = low + (high-low)//2.
Binary search in a sorted array, implement lower bound, implement upper bound.
The DOM: querySelector, traversal, createElement, appendChild, textContent vs innerHTML (and XSS).
Boundary variants: search insert position, floor and ceiling. Off-by-one is the whole game here.
Search insert position, floor and ceil in a sorted array.
Events: addEventListener, the event object, bubbling and capturing, delegation, preventDefault.
First and last occurrence. Counting occurrences as two boundary searches.
First and last occurrence of a number, count occurrences of a number.
Forms and validation in JS. Building and updating lists in the DOM. Template literals for markup.
Rotated sorted arrays: identify which half is sorted, then decide where the target can be.
Search in rotated sorted array I, search in rotated sorted array II (with duplicates).
Build a to-do app: add, edit, delete, filter, persist to localStorage. Vanilla JS only.
Finding the rotation point. Minimum in a rotated array.
Minimum in rotated sorted array, find how many times an array is rotated.
Continue the to-do app: keyboard support, empty states, no-JS fallback. Make it actually good.
Binary search where the array isn't fully sorted: peaks and pairs.
Single element in a sorted array, find peak element.
Debugging: Chrome DevTools, breakpoints, the network tab, console methods beyond log.
sun: Write the binary search template from memory three separate times today. It has to be automatic before we hit binary-search-on-answers.
Core CS: DBMS — what a database is, tables, schemas, primary/foreign keys.

weeks.goal: Binary search on the answer space is the single most under-recognised pattern in interviews. Learn to spot it.
d: Searching the answer space, not the array. The shape: minimise the maximum, or maximise the minimum.
Square root of a number, Nth root of a number.
The event loop, call stack, task queue. Why JS is single-threaded but not blocking.
Designing the feasibility function: can we do it in X? Then binary search on X.
Koko eating bananas, minimum days to make M bouquets.
Callbacks → promises → async/await. Promise.all, Promise.race, error handling in async code.
More answer-space problems. Recognising the monotonic predicate.
Smallest divisor given a threshold, capacity to ship packages within D days.
fetch: GET, POST, headers, status codes, CORS. Working with a real public API.
Allocation and partition problems — the hardest common form of this pattern.
Aggressive cows, book allocation.
Build a weather or movie-search app against a real API. Loading states, error states, empty states.
Split array largest sum, painter's partition, and the median of two sorted arrays.
Split array largest sum, painter's partition, median of two sorted arrays (the hard one).
Continue the API app: debounced search, pagination, caching responses, abort controllers.
Treating a 2D matrix as a flattened 1D array. Staircase search for row-and-column sorted matrices.
Row with maximum 1s, search in a 2D matrix, search in a 2D matrix II, peak element in 2D.
ES6+ round-up: optional chaining, nullish coalescing, generators, Map and Set. Ship the API app.
sun: Re-solve Koko eating bananas and aggressive cows cold. They are the same problem in different clothes — make sure you can see that.
Core CS: DBMS — ER modelling, normalisation 1NF → 2NF → 3NF, when to denormalise.

weeks.goal: Python makes strings easy, which is a trap. Know the cost of what you're writing.
d: Python strings: immutability, why += in a loop is O(n²), join(), and the common methods.
Remove outermost parentheses, reverse words in a string.
Plan a real project — pick something you'd actually use. Wireframe it. Write a spec before coding.
Sorting and comparing strings. Custom comparators for string problems.
Largest odd number in a string, longest common prefix, isomorphic strings.
Build: structure, state model, core interactions. Vanilla JS, no framework.
Anagram and rotation checks. Grouping with a hashmap of sorted keys.
Valid anagram, rotate string, group anagrams.
Build: connect to an API or localStorage. Handle every failure case.
Frequency-driven string problems.
Sort characters by frequency, maximum nesting depth of parentheses.
Build: responsive layout, accessibility pass, keyboard navigation.
Roman numerals both ways. atoi — the string-to-integer edge cases interviewers love.
Roman to integer, integer to Roman, string to integer (atoi).
Build: polish, empty states, error messages that say what to do next.
Expand-around-centre for palindromes. Two pointers on strings.
Longest palindromic substring, sum of beauty of all substrings.
Deploy it. Write the README. Record a 60-second demo GIF for the repo.
sun: Month 2 done. Re-solve one problem each from arrays, binary search and strings, all cold. Check your revision backlog.
Core CS: DBMS — SQL basics. SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY, GROUP BY, HAVING, the join types.

weeks.goal: Linked list problems are pure pointer discipline. Draw the boxes and arrows on paper. Every single time.
d: The Node class, building a list from an array, traversal. Why a linked list over an array, and when not.
Build a linked list from an array, find its length, search for an element.
Ep 01 Inception. VS Code setup, hello world in HTML/JS, React via CDN links, createElement. Why React needs a build setup at all.
Insertion and deletion at head, tail, and the kth position. The dummy-head trick.
Delete head, delete tail, delete kth node, insert at head/tail/position.
Ep 02 Igniting our App. npm, package.json, Parcel, node_modules, .gitignore, browserslist, dev vs production builds.
Doubly linked lists: maintaining prev, and the edge cases that break naive code.
Build a DLL, insert and delete in a DLL, reverse a DLL.
Ep 03 Laying the foundation. JSX and how Babel transpiles it, React components, functional vs class, component composition.
The slow and fast pointer. Why it finds the middle, and why it detects cycles.
Middle of a linked list, detect a loop in a linked list.
Ep 03 assignments. Nested components, JSX expressions, props. Do every assignment — the whole course is built on them.
Floyd's cycle detection: proving where the two pointers meet, and finding the loop start.
Starting point of the loop, length of the loop.
Ep 04 Talk is Cheap, Show Me the Code. Start Namaste Food: plan the app, Header, Body, RestaurantCard, props.
Reversal, iterative and recursive. This one problem underpins ten others.
Reverse a linked list (both ways), check if a linked list is a palindrome.
Ep 04 continued. Map over the Swiggy dummy data API, keys and why they matter, optional chaining on API responses.
sun: Reverse a linked list from a blank file, iteratively and recursively, three times. This is the most-asked linked list question there is.
Core CS: DBMS — transactions and ACID. Isolation levels and the anomalies each one prevents.

weeks.goal: Reverse-in-groups-of-K is the hardest pointer manipulation you'll be asked. Everything here builds to it.
d: Segregation and rearrangement by relinking, not by swapping values.
Odd-even linked list, segregate 0s, 1s and 2s in a linked list.
Ep 05 Let's Get Hooked. Folder structure, named vs default exports, useState, and why React re-renders.
The two-pointer gap technique for finding the nth node from the end.
Remove nth node from the end, delete the middle node.
Ep 05 assignments. Add search and filter to the restaurant list. Understand exactly what state triggers a render.
Merge sort on a linked list — why it's the right sort here and quicksort isn't.
Sort a linked list, sort 0s/1s/2s without swapping data.
Ep 06 Exploring the World. Monolith vs microservices, useEffect, real API calls, shimmer UI instead of a spinner.
Two-list problems: intersection, and adding numbers stored as lists.
Intersection of two linked lists, add two numbers represented as linked lists.
Ep 6.1 and 6.2 — the Swiggy API and CORS fixes. Then conditional rendering and the online-status pattern.
Reversing in groups of K — the hardest common linked list problem. Plus rotation.
Reverse a linked list in groups of K, rotate a linked list.
Ep 07 Finding the Path. React Router DOM, createBrowserRouter, children routes, Outlet, Link vs anchor tag.
Deep-copying a list with random pointers. Flattening a multi-level list.
Clone a linked list with random pointers, flatten a linked list.
Ep 07 continued. Dynamic routing with useParams, the restaurant menu page, errorElement and useRouteError.
sun: Re-solve reverse-in-groups-of-K cold. If you can write it without hesitation, linked lists are done.
Core CS: DBMS — indexing, B-trees, what makes a query slow, reading a query plan.

weeks.goal: The take / not-take decision tree is the foundation of both backtracking and dynamic programming. Do not rush this week.
d: Recursion as a decision tree: at every element, take it or don't. Drawing the tree before coding.
Generate all subsequences of an array, print subsequences with sum K.
Ep 08 Let's Get Classy. Class components, constructor, props and state in classes. You will meet these in legacy code.
Return-type recursion (returns a value) vs void recursion (mutates shared state). When each fits.
Count subsequences with sum K, check if any subsequence sums to K (early exit).
Ep 08 continued. Lifecycle: componentDidMount, componentDidUpdate, componentWillUnmount — and how each maps onto useEffect.
Combination problems: reusing elements vs not, and how the recursive call index changes.
Combination Sum I, Combination Sum II (handling duplicates).
Ep 09 Optimizing our App. Custom hooks: useRestaurantMenu, useOnlineStatus. One responsibility per hook.
Subsets and duplicate handling — sorting first, then skipping equal siblings.
Subset sum I, subset sum II, subsets II.
Ep 09 continued. Code splitting, lazy loading, Suspense, chunking. Why bundle size is a real product concern.
Fixed-size combinations, and mapping digits to letters.
Combination Sum III, letter combinations of a phone number.
Ep 10 Jo Dikhta Hai, Vo Bikta Hai. Tailwind with Parcel, config, utility-first thinking.
Recursion on strings. Permutations without duplicates.
String permutations, merge sort written recursively from scratch.
Ep 10 continued. Style all of Namaste Food in Tailwind. Responsive breakpoints, mobile-first.
sun: Draw the full recursion tree for Combination Sum II on paper. Trace three branches by hand, including the duplicate-skip.
Core CS: DBMS wrap-up. Write and run 20 SQL queries against a sample database.

weeks.goal: Backtracking is recursion plus an undo step. If you can write N-Queens from scratch, you own it.
d: Backtracking: the choose / explore / un-choose loop. Why restoring state matters.
Palindrome partitioning, word search in a grid.
Ep 11 Data is the New Oil. Higher-order components, controlled vs uncontrolled components.
Grid backtracking with a visited set and direction arrays.
Rat in a maze, N-Queens (find one solution).
Ep 11 continued. Lifting state up, props drilling and its real cost, Context API with useContext, React DevTools.
Constraint satisfaction and pruning — checking validity before recursing, not after.
N-Queens (print all solutions), M-colouring problem.
Ep 12 Let's Build Our Store. Redux Toolkit: store, slice, reducers, actions. Why Redux rather than Context.
Sudoku: the constraint checks and why pruning order changes the runtime by orders of magnitude.
Sudoku solver, word break (recursive form).
Ep 12 continued. useSelector, useDispatch, build the cart feature. Immutability and what RTK handles for you.
Building expressions recursively. Partitioning strings with operators.
Expression add operators, maximum score from removing substrings.
Ep 13 Time for Test. Jest setup with Parcel, React Testing Library, Babel config, jsdom.
Powerset via recursion, and finding the kth permutation without generating all of them.
Powerset, kth permutation sequence.
Ep 13 continued. Unit and integration tests, fireEvent, mocking fetch. Then the bonus episode: useMemo, useCallback, useRef.
sun: Write N-Queens from a blank file. If you can, backtracking is yours. If you can't, that's this Sunday's job.
Core CS: OS — processes vs threads, context switching, what the kernel actually does.

weeks.goal: A short, high-yield week. Bit tricks show up in DP-with-bitmask later, so this isn't optional.
d: Binary representation, two's complement. AND, OR, XOR, NOT, left and right shift.
Convert decimal to binary and back, swap two numbers using XOR.
Ep 14 NetflixGPT begins. Project setup, Firebase auth, login and signup form, validation with useRef.
Check, set, clear and toggle the ith bit. Removing the last set bit with n & (n-1).
Check the ith bit, set/clear/toggle the ith bit, remove the last set bit.
Ep 14 continued. Redux user slice, protected routes, sign out, updateProfile. Auth state as a single source of truth.
Counting set bits. Brian Kernighan's algorithm. Powers of two in one operation.
Count set bits, check if a number is a power of two, minimum bits to flip A to B.
Ep 15 Building the Core. TMDB API, a custom hook per movie list, the Redux movies slice.
XOR properties: x^x=0, x^0=x, and commutativity. The whole single-number family falls out of this.
Single number I, single number II, single number III.
Ep 15 continued. Main container, video background with trailer, secondary container, movie carousels.
Generating subsets with a bitmask. XOR over a range in O(1).
Power set using bit manipulation, XOR of numbers in a range L to R.
Ep 16 Wrapping Up. The GPT search feature, OpenAI API integration, .env files for secret keys.
Number theory: sieve-based prime factorisation, modular exponentiation, modular inverse basics.
Sieve of Eratosthenes, prime factors using a sieve, power(a,b,mod), count all divisors.
Ep 16 continued. Multi-language support, memoisation for expensive renders, deploy to Firebase or Vercel.
sun: Month 3 done. Re-solve one linked list problem and one backtracking problem cold. Audit your revision backlog seriously.
Core CS: OS — CPU scheduling: FCFS, SJF, round robin, priority. Compute waiting times by hand.

weeks.goal: We use PostgreSQL rather than MongoDB. SQL is its own interview round at product companies. Mongo is not.
d: Stack and queue: LIFO and FIFO. Python list vs collections.deque, and why deque for queues.
Implement a stack using an array, implement a queue using an array.
Bonus: Machine Coding Interview. How the round actually runs, and how to break down a UI in the first ten minutes.
Implementing one structure with the other — the classic interview warm-up.
Stack using queues, queue using stacks.
Build Namaste YouTube: head, sidebar, video container, YouTube API, shimmer UI.
Stack and queue backed by a linked list. Comparing to array-backed versions.
Stack using a linked list, queue using a linked list.
Live search with autocomplete. Debouncing and caching API responses — the most-asked machine coding feature there is.
Balanced brackets. The theory of infix, prefix and postfix notation.
Valid parentheses, convert infix to postfix.
Nested comments. Recursive components, and why this specific question separates candidates.
The remaining notation conversions. Every one is a stack traversal with different rules.
Postfix to infix, prefix to infix, postfix to prefix.
Live chat with anonymous messages, and infinite scroll on the video feed.
Evaluating expressions with a stack. Operator precedence and associativity.
Evaluate postfix expression, prefix to postfix, infix to prefix.
Advanced features and wrap-up. Deploy, write the README, record a demo of the YouTube clone.
sun: Write infix-to-postfix from memory. It's a guaranteed question in Indian product-company and campus interviews.
Core CS: OS — deadlock (the four conditions), mutexes, semaphores, producer-consumer.

weeks.goal: The monotonic stack turns O(n²) into O(n). Once you see the pattern, a dozen hard problems become routine.
d: The monotonic stack: maintaining increasing or decreasing order, and why each element is pushed and popped once.
Next greater element I, next greater element II (circular).
Ep 00 Welcome + Ep 01 Introduction to Node.js. What Node actually is, its history, and why JS on the server changed things.
Next and previous smaller element. Choosing the direction of the scan.
Next smaller element, number of next-greater-elements to the right.
Ep 02 JS on Server + Ep 03 Let's write code. V8, ECMAScript, and your first server-side JavaScript.
The contribution technique: for each element, how many subarrays is it the minimum of?
Sum of subarray minimums, sum of subarray ranges.
Ep 04 module.export & require. CommonJS vs ES modules, module scope, the IIFE wrapper, the five steps of require.
The histogram pattern — previous smaller and next smaller combined.
Largest rectangle in a histogram, maximal rectangle in a binary matrix.
Ep 05 Diving into the Node.js GitHub repo. Reading real source code — a skill worth more than the episode itself.
Trapping rain water: brute force, prefix arrays, then two pointers. Understand all three.
Trapping rainwater, asteroid collision.
Ep 06 libuv & async IO. Sync vs async, blocking vs non-blocking, and what libuv is actually doing underneath.
Stack-based greedy: removing digits, and the stock span problem. LRU cache design.
Stock span problem, remove K digits, LRU cache.
Ep 07 sync, async, setTimeoutZero. Call stack, callback queue, and why setTimeout(fn, 0) is not immediate.
sun: Largest rectangle in a histogram, cold. It appears constantly and it's the purest test of the monotonic stack idea.
Core CS: OS — memory management, paging, segmentation, virtual memory. Then the Resume Masterclass (course bonus) and a first draft.

weeks.goal: Four window shapes cover almost everything: fixed size, variable size, count-the-subarrays, and window-with-a-structure.
d: The variable-size window: expand right, shrink left while the condition breaks.
Longest substring without repeating characters.
Ep 08 Deep dive into the V8 engine. Parsing, Ignition, TurboFan, JIT compilation, garbage collection.
Windows with a counter of violations rather than a set.
Max consecutive ones III, fruit into baskets.
Ep 09 libuv & the Event Loop. The six phases: timers, pending callbacks, idle/prepare, poll, check, close.
At-most-K-distinct windows using a frequency map.
Longest substring with at most K distinct characters, number of substrings containing all three characters.
Ep 09 continued. process.nextTick vs promise microtasks vs setImmediate vs setTimeout. Learn this cold — it is the most-asked Node question.
The at-most trick: exactly(K) = atMost(K) − atMost(K−1). This converts hard counting into easy counting.
Binary subarrays with sum, count number of nice subarrays.
Ep 10 Thread pool in libuv. UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE, and which operations actually use the pool: fs, dns, crypto, zlib.
Windows where the condition needs the max frequency inside it.
Longest repeating character replacement, maximum points you can obtain from cards.
Ep 11 Creating a Server. The http module, sockets, TCP vs HTTP, handling req and res without Express.
Windows that need an auxiliary structure — a deque for max, a counter for coverage.
Minimum window substring, sliding window maximum.
Ep 12 SQL vs NoSQL + Ep 13 Creating a database with MongoDB. Atlas setup, Compass, CRUD, when each database type fits.
sun: Month 4 done. Re-solve minimum window substring cold. It combines hashing, two pointers and careful bookkeeping.
Core CS: OS wrap-up — 30 interview questions with written answers. Then the LinkedIn Masterclass and rewrite your profile.

weeks.goal: Python's heapq is a min-heap only. Learn the negation trick for max-heaps now, before you need it under pressure.
d: The heap property, sift-up and sift-down, why building a heap is O(n) not O(n log n).
Implement a min-heap and a max-heap from scratch, with push, pop and heapify.
S2 Ep 00 Introduction to Project + Ep 01 Microservices vs Monolith. Which to choose, with the real trade-offs.
Heap sort. Verifying the heap property. Python's heapq and the negation trick for max-heaps.
Heap sort, check if an array represents a min-heap, convert a min-heap to a max-heap.
Ep 02 Features, HLD & LLD planning. Do this one properly — it is directly reusable in your LLD interview round.
The top-K pattern: keep a heap of size K, not a heap of size N.
Kth largest element, kth smallest element, top K frequent elements.
Ep 03 Creating our Express Server. Init, listen, nodemon, and why route order matters.
Merging K sorted sequences with a heap of heads.
Merge K sorted arrays, merge K sorted linked lists.
Ep 04 Routing and Request Handlers. Route params, query strings, dynamic and regex routes.
Greedy scheduling with a heap — the pattern behind task and interval scheduling.
Task scheduler, hands of straights.
Ep 05 Middlewares & Error Handlers. app.use, next(), the error middleware signature, tracing the request flow.
Two heaps for a running median. Distance-based top-K.
Find median from a data stream, K closest points to origin, minimum operations to halve array sum.
Ep 06 Schema & Models with Mongoose + Ep 07 Diving into the APIs. Signup, login, your first CRUD endpoints.
sun: Implement a heap from scratch again, no reference. Then explain out loud why build-heap is O(n).

weeks.goal: Graphs are the biggest step in the sheet. BFS and DFS templates first — forty problems are built on them.
